## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Working backwards from a design to its data requirements: unit of observation, level of aggregation, time frequency, span, coverage, and which comparisons the data has to contain. Can this be done with county-level data, or does it need individuals? Then the landscape — administrative records, official statistics, firm and platform data — and what each costs in money and time

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Research ethics, the Cornell IRB, and data-use agreements: what needs approval, what does not, and how long it takes. Then work out whether your own project needs it — while there is still time to change course

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
